references.text: The names of the tribal leaders appointed to help Moses with the census. These are the same leaders who now bring offerings.
Refers to those who 'were over the counted,' that is, the tribal leaders who led the census together with Moses and Aaron.
Describes the role of the tribal leaders as heads over their respective camps and tribes.
The princes brought precious stones and other materials for the tabernacle, a similar example of the generosity of the leaders.
The princes, heads of Israel's thousands, are gathered when the trumpets sound, showing their leadership role.
Each tribal leader was to give a staff with his name, confirming their role as 'heads of fathers' houses'.
